title: Quasi-affineness can be checked on an affine target cover
statement: Let $h:Z\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $S=\bigcup_{a\in A}S_a$ be an affine open cover. A quasi-affine scheme means a scheme isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme, where quasi-compact means that every open covering admits a finite subcover. Then $h$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism] if and only if $h^{-1}(S_a)$ is a quasi-affine scheme for every $a\in A$. No quasi-compactness or separation hypothesis on $S$ and no finite-type hypothesis on $h$ is imposed.

proof.text: The forward implication is immediate from [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]: if $h$ is quasi-affine, then the inverse image of every affine open of $S$, in particular each $S_a$, is a quasi-affine scheme.

Assume that every $Z_a=h^{-1}(S_a)$ is quasi-affine. By [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding], each $Z_a$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The restricted map $h_a:Z_a\to S_a$ is therefore quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) (its target is affine and hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]); applying [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] to the affine cover $(S_a)$ gives that $h$ is quasi-compact. To see that $h$ is quasi-separated, cover $Z\times_S Z$ by the opens $Z_a\times_{S_a}Z_a$. The inverse image of the $a$-th open under the diagonal is $Z_a$, and the restricted diagonal is the diagonal of $h_a$, which is quasi-compact because $h_a$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). The same target-local criterion [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] applied to $\Delta_h$ makes $\Delta_h$ quasi-compact; by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], $h$ is quasi-separated. (If the cover is empty, then $S$ and $Z$ are empty and the conclusion is vacuous.)

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-relative-affinization-compatible-charts] to the quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism $h$. It provides the quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal A=h_*\mathcal O_Z$, an affine relative spectrum $\pi:Y\to S$, and compatible maps $e_a:Z_a\to Y_a=\pi^{-1}(S_a)$ over $S_a$. In its specified chart $Y_a\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(Z_a,\mathcal O_{Z_a})$, each $e_a$ is the canonical map $j_a$.

Each $Z_a$ is quasi-compact and its canonical map $j_a$ is an open immersion by [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding]. Since $q_a\circ e_a=j_a$ with $q_a:Y_a\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(Z_a,\mathcal O_{Z_a})$ the chart isomorphism of step 3, $e_a=q_a^{-1}\circ j_a$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]: it identifies $Z_a$ with an open subscheme of $Y_a$. Thus all the hypotheses of [lem-a1-affine-base-open-immersion-gluing] hold for the compatible $e_a$ and the affine map $\pi$. It gives a quasi-compact open immersion $c:Z\to Y$ with $\pi\circ c=h$, restricting to the prescribed $e_a$ on the cover.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, proof of (2) implies (4), final assertion

proof.text: For any affine open $U\subseteq S$, the relative-Spec chart in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2) makes $Y_U=\pi^{-1}(U)$ affine. Since $c$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and $\pi c=h$, the inverse image $h^{-1}(U)=c^{-1}(Y_U)$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme of the affine scheme $Y_U$. By [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism], this is exactly that $h$ is quasi-affine.
